category: Semiconductor Module: Semiconductor, Schrödinger and Optoelectronics Interfaces
description: Domain, boundary and subnode features of the Semiconductor (semi) interface (material model, doping, traps, generation–recombination, mobility models, contacts, gates, heterojunctions, tunneling, optical transitions), the Schrödinger Equation (schr) and Schrödinger–Poisson interfaces, the optoelectronics multiphysics interfaces, and Semiconductor Module study steps and variables, from the COMSOL 6.4 Semiconductor Module User's Guide. Java type strings were verified against the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Semiconductor Material Model (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Default domain node of the Semiconductor interface that adds Poisson's equation and the electron/hole drift–diffusion equations and holds the material data: relative permittivity, band gap Eg0 (default 1.12 V, entered as energy/e), electron affinity chi0 (4.05 V), effective densities of states Nc and Nv, and electron/hole mobilities that can be overridden by mobility-model subnodes. It also sets band gap narrowing, dopant ionization (complete/incomplete) and, for the Semiconductor Equilibrium step, the equilibrium condition (Bias voltage or Total charge).
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Semiconductor Material Model 1 (default). Java: physics("semi").feature("smm1") (type SemiconductorMaterialModel); set("BandGapNarrowing", "slotboom"); set("Ionization", "incomplete")

parameters.name: epsilonr, Eg0, chi0, Nc, Nv
parameters.description: Material properties (From material; Semiconductor material library).

parameters.name: mun, mup
parameters.description: Electron and hole mobilities or outputs of mobility subnodes (e.g. semi.mun_ct).

parameters.name: BandGapNarrowing
parameters.description: none, slotboom, jain (Jain–Roulston) or user defined.

parameters.name: Ionization
parameters.description: complete or incomplete (deltaEd, deltaEa, degeneracy factors gd, ga).

parameters.name: EquilibriumCondition
parameters.description: Bias_voltage (V0_bias) or total charge (Q0_tot) for Semiconductor Equilibrium.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/pn_junction_1d: silicon Semiconductor Material Model with Analytic Doping Models and Metal Contacts, voltage sweep of the I-V curve.
tools.notes: Mobility subnodes: User-Defined, Power Law (L), Fletcher (C), Caughey–Thomas (E), Lombardi (S), Arora (LI), Klaassen (LIC). Band gap and affinity are in volts so that eV values can be typed directly.

tools.name: Semiconductor discretization and formulation options
tools.description: Discretization setting of the Semiconductor interface: Finite volume (constant shape function, default; best current conservation), Finite element log formulation (linear or quadratic; fewer DOFs, recommended for 3D), Finite element quasi-Fermi level (linear/quadratic; wide band gap or cryogenic devices), Finite element density-gradient (linear/quadratic; quantum confinement corrections with Slotboom variables) and Mixed finite element log formulation (leakage currents in highly doped reverse-biased devices). Streamline diffusion stabilization is available for the FE log formulations.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Settings > Discretization > Formulation (Show More Options > Stabilization for streamline diffusion)

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: Finite volume, FE log (linear/quadratic), FE quasi Fermi level, FE density-gradient, Mixed FE log.

parameters.name: Value type when using splitting of complex variables
Dependent variables
parameters.description: V, N, P (log or quasi-Fermi level forms; Slotboom variables for density-gradient).

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/insb_pfet_density_gradient and nanowire_density_gradient_3d use the density-gradient formulation; Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/reverse_bias_leakage_current illustrates leakage calculation.
tools.notes: See 'Discretization and Formulation Options' in the Semiconductor User's Guide; finite volume needs a mesh aligned with junctions for best accuracy.

tools.name: Carrier statistics, incomplete ionization and band gap narrowing (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Physics options of the Semiconductor interface: Carrier statistics Maxwell–Boltzmann (default; quasi-Fermi levels well inside the gap) or Fermi–Dirac (degenerate semiconductors); Solution Electrons and holes (default) or Majority carriers only (other carrier from np = ni^2); continuation parameters that ramp doping and trap densities for convergence; a Reference temperature for energy levels T0 (default 293.15 K) that fixes the equilibrium Fermi level as 0 eV; plus, in the material model, incomplete ionization of dopants and Slotboom or Jain–Roulston band gap narrowing.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Settings > Model Properties (Carrier statistics, Solution), Continuation Settings, Reference Temperature (advanced); Semiconductor Material Model > Band Gap Narrowing / Dopant Ionization

parameters.name: Solution
parameters.description: Electrons and holes or Majority carriers only (Electrons/Holes).

parameters.name: Interface continuation parameter Cp
parameters.description: Default 1; doping and trap density continuation options.

tools.example: Heavily doped emitter: set Carrier statistics = Fermi–Dirac, Band gap narrowing = Slotboom and Ionization = incomplete, then sweep the continuation parameter from 0 to 1 to converge.
tools.notes: Band gap and electron affinity inputs are in V (numerically equal to eV).

tools.name: Analytic Doping Model (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Defines acceptor or donor doping in terms of the (local) coordinate system: User defined expression (default) or Box distribution with a uniform region (Base corner/center, width/depth/height) outside which the concentration decays to a background level Nb with a Gaussian, Linear or Error-function profile set by junction depth, decay length, gradient or argument factor. Plot Doping Profile buttons preview the net doping before solving.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Analytic Doping Model. Java: physics("semi").create("adm1", "AnalyticDopingModel", 2); set("impurityDistribution", "box"); set("impurityType", "donor"); set("NDc", "1e18[1/cm^3]"); set("JunctionOrLength", "junction_depth")

parameters.name: dropoff_profile, JunctionOrLength, jds, ls, Nb
parameters.description: Profile (gaussian, linear, erf), junction depth/decay length and background doping.

parameters.name: ContinuationType
parameters.description: Use the interface continuation parameter or a user-defined one.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/pn_junction_1d: p-type background plus a Gaussian n+ box with junction depth 1 um.
tools.notes: Several doping nodes add up; semi.Nnetdop gives the net doping. For profiles defined by distance from surfaces use Geometric Doping Model.

tools.name: Geometric Doping Model with Boundary Selection for Doping Profile (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Defines doping as a function of the distance D from selected boundaries (default Boundary Selection for Doping Profile subnode), so profiles follow curved or angled surfaces and survive geometry changes. Profile away from the boundary: Gaussian (default), Linear, Error function or User defined N(D) using semi.gdm#.D; the concentration at the boundary and the junction depth or length scale set the decay.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Geometric Doping Model > Boundary Selection for Doping Profile. Java: physics("semi").create("gdm1", "GeometricDopingModel", 2); feature("gdm1").feature("gdmbs1").selection().set(new int[]{...})

parameters.name: impurityProfile
parameters.description: gaussian, linear, erf_func or user defined (UserDefinedProfile).

parameters.name: impurityType, NAgen / NDgen
parameters.description: Dopant type and concentration at the boundary.

parameters.name: JunctionOrLength, jd_gen, l_gen, Nb_gen
parameters.description: Junction depth or decay length and background concentration.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Applications/si_solar_cell_with_ray_optics and Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/gaas_pin_photodiode: emitter doping diffused from the top surface.
tools.notes: Distance computation is geometric; use a fine mesh near the selected boundaries to resolve steep profiles.

tools.name: Analytic / Geometric Trap Density (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Nodes that define a spatially varying density of trap states in a domain, used together with Trap-Assisted Recombination (explicit traps) to describe defects whose concentration varies in space. Analytic Trap Density uses coordinate expressions or a uniform box decaying to a background with preset profiles (as Analytic Doping Model); Geometric Trap Density uses the distance from boundaries picked in a Boundary Selection for Trap Density Profile subnode. Continuation settings ramp trap densities for convergence.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Analytic Trap Density / Geometric Trap Density (> Boundary Selection for Trap Density Profile)

parameters.name: Distribution
parameters.description: User defined or Box (analytic); Gaussian/Linear/erf/user-defined decay (geometric).

parameters.name: Trap type
parameters.description: Donor traps (default), Acceptor traps, Neutral electron traps or Neutral hole traps.

parameters.name: Continuation
parameters.description: Interface continuation parameter or user defined.

tools.example: Radiation-damaged region below the surface of a detector: Geometric Trap Density decaying from the entrance window, referenced by an explicit Trap-Assisted Recombination node.
tools.notes: Java type strings not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Trap-Assisted Recombination (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Generation–recombination node for indirect band-gap materials such as silicon (an expanded version of the old Shockley–Read–Hall node). Domain trapping model Shockley–Read–Hall (default; lifetimes taun/taup From material, user-defined default 10 us, trap level offset Delta_Et from the intrinsic level) or Explicit trap distribution, which adds trap-occupancy DOFs for discrete and continuous trap levels (with donor/acceptor/neutral trap species) via Discrete Energy Level and Continuous Energy Levels subnodes, including trap charge in Poisson's equation.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Generation–Recombination > Trap-Assisted Recombination. Java: physics("semi").create("tar1", "TrapAssistedRecombination", 2); set("IncludeTraps", "SRHModel"); set("taun", "1[us]"); set("taup", "1[us]")

parameters.name: taun, taup, Delta_Et
parameters.description: Carrier lifetimes and trap level offset from midgap (SRH).

parameters.name: SpecifyTrapSpecies / SpecifyDiscreteContinuous
parameters.description: Enable trap species and continuous/discrete levels (explicit).

parameters.name: TrappingFormulation
parameters.description: Trap occupancy or trap quasi-Fermi level (density-gradient).

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/pin_reverse_recovery (SRH) and Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/nanowire_traps (explicit traps).
tools.notes: Surface/interface variants: Trap-Assisted Surface Recombination and Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination.

tools.name: Discrete Energy Level / Transition Between Discrete Levels (Semiconductor traps)
tools.description: Subnodes of Trap-Assisted Recombination (domains), Trap-Assisted Surface Recombination (boundaries) and Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination when Explicit trap distribution is used. Discrete Energy Level defines one trap level: trap type (donor, acceptor, neutral electron, neutral hole), energy relative to the conduction/valence band or midgap, degeneracy, number density and electron/hole capture probabilities (from cross sections and thermal velocities or user defined). Transition Between Discrete Levels adds carrier transitions between two such levels, e.g. quantum-dot/well intermediate-band models.
tools.usage: Trap-Assisted Recombination (Explicit trap distribution) > Discrete Energy Level / Transition Between Discrete Levels. Java: feature("tar1").create("dtd1", "DiscreteEnergyLevelDomain", 2); boundary: "DiscreteEnergyLevelBoundary"; transitions: "TransitionBetweenDiscreteLevelsDomain"

parameters.name: Et0in / DistributionCenterPoint
parameters.description: Trap energy and its reference (from conduction band, midgap...).

parameters.name: sigman, sigmap, vn_th, vp_th / Cnin, Cpin
parameters.description: Capture cross sections and thermal velocities or capture probabilities.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/dot_in_well_solar_cell: discrete levels for dots and wells with Transition Between Discrete Levels and user rate terms.
tools.notes: Trapped charge is included in Poisson's equation automatically.

tools.name: Continuous Energy Levels (Semiconductor traps)
tools.description: Subnode for a continuous density of trap states within the band gap (domains, boundaries or heterointerfaces) when explicit traps with continuous levels are selected. Trap density distribution: Gaussian (width 0.333 V default), Rectangle (width and transition zone), Exponential (damping coefficient) or User defined g_t(E), with trap number density Nt (default 1e12 1/cm^3), energy center and capture parameters; the energy integral is discretized in an extra dimension.
tools.usage: Trap-Assisted (Surface) Recombination > Continuous Energy Levels. Java: feature("tasr1").create("ctb1", "ContinuousEnergyLevelsBoundary", 1)

parameters.name: Edisc
parameters.description: Number of discretization points in the energy extra dimension.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/moscap_1d_interface_traps: Gaussian acceptor/donor interface-trap distributions at the Si/SiO2 interface broaden the C-V curve.
tools.notes: Used with Semiconductor Equilibrium and Small-Signal studies for C-V/G-V analysis.

tools.name: Trap-Assisted Surface Recombination (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Boundary condition adding surface recombination and interface-trap charge on semiconductor surfaces and semiconductor–insulator interfaces: Shockley–Read–Hall surface model with recombination velocities vsn, vsp (default 1000 cm/s) or explicit discrete/continuous trap levels. It replaces the Surface traps checkbox of pre-5.4 Insulator Interface and can be combined with Ideal Schottky Metal Contacts.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Boundaries > Trap-Assisted Surface Recombination. Java: physics("semi").create("tasr1", "TrapAssistedSurfaceRecombination", 1); set("IncludeTraps", "ExplicitTraps")

parameters.name: SpecifyDiscreteContinuous
parameters.description: Discrete only or continuous and/or discrete levels.

parameters.name: TrappingFormulation / TrappingFormulationDG
parameters.description: Trap occupancy or trap quasi-Fermi level.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/inas_nanowire_traps_hysteresis_density_gradient: surface traps cause gate-sweep hysteresis.
tools.notes: Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination offers only the explicit model at heterojunctions.

tools.name: Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Boundary condition for recombination and trapped charge at heterojunctions, adding contributions to the interface recombination rate and interface charge for the Continuity/Heterojunction condition (not for the Continuous quasi-Fermi levels option). Settings match Trap-Assisted Surface Recombination except that only the Explicit trap distribution is available, because the recombination draws carriers from both sides of the junction.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Boundaries > Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination (on Continuity/Heterojunction boundaries with thermionic emission or user-defined current)

parameters.name: Discrete / Continuous Energy Levels (Heterointerfaces)
parameters.description: Trap levels and densities at the interface.

tools.example: GaN/AlGaN heterostructure LED: Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination with a discrete acceptor level at each quantum-well interface.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Auger Recombination (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Generation–recombination node for band-to-band Auger recombination at high carrier densities, R = (Cn*n + Cp*p)(n*p - gamma_n*gamma_p*ni_eff^2), with coefficients Cn and Cp (defaults for silicon 2.8e-31 and 9.9e-32 cm^6/s, From material). Important in heavily doped regions, high-injection power devices, LEDs and lasers.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Generation–Recombination > Auger Recombination. Java: physics("semi").create("aur1", "AURecombination", 2); set("Cn", "2.8e-31[cm^6/s]")
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/gaas_pn_junction_infrared_led_diode and gan_double_heterostructure_led (efficiency droop from Auger).
tools.notes: Combine with Direct Recombination (radiative) and Trap-Assisted Recombination; rates add.

tools.name: Direct Recombination (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Generation–recombination node for direct (radiative band-to-band) recombination in direct band-gap materials such as GaAs, R = C(n*p - gamma_n*gamma_p*Nc0*Nv0*exp(-(Eg - dEg)/Vth)), with the Direct recombination factor C (m^3/s) From material (default 0). For spectrally resolved emission and gain use Optical Transitions instead.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Generation–Recombination > Direct Recombination
tools.example: GaAs pn diode: Direct Recombination with C = 7.2e-10 cm^3/s plus SRH to reproduce the ideality factor transition.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Impact Ionization Generation (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Generation node for avalanche multiplication, G = (alpha_n*|Jn| + alpha_p*|Jp|)/q, where the ionization coefficients are User defined or from the Okuto–Crowell model driven by the field component parallel to each current (parameters an, ap, bn, bp, cn, cp, dn, dp, Tref). An optional Indirect update of the generation rate adds DOFs so the rate can lag one step via a Previous Solution node, aiding convergence near breakdown.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Generation–Recombination > Impact Ionization Generation. Java: physics("semi").create("iig1", "IIGeneration", 2); set("iiG_model", "OkutoCrowellModel")

parameters.name: an, ap, bn, bp, cnii, cpii, dn, dp

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/sic_diode_breakdown and Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/mosfet_breakdown (reverse-bias sweep to avalanche).
tools.notes: Use small voltage steps, current-driven contacts near breakdown, and fine meshes in high-field regions.

tools.name: User-Defined Recombination / Generation (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Generation–recombination nodes where arbitrary expressions set the net recombination (Rn, Rp) or generation (Gn, Gp) rates of electrons and holes, e.g. optical generation computed by ray optics or Beer–Lambert, radiation-induced generation, or band-to-band tunneling models. Electron and hole rates can differ (for trapping or unipolar sources).
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Generation–Recombination > User-Defined Generation (type UDGeneration) / User-Defined Recombination (type UDRecombination). Java: physics("semi").create("udg1", "UDGeneration", 2); set("Gn", "G_ph"); set("Gp", "G_ph")
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Applications/si_solar_cell_with_ray_optics (photogeneration from ray tracing), Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/pin_radiation_effects and Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/tunnel_diode.
tools.notes: Generation terms are positive sources; recombination terms are positive sinks.

tools.name: Power Law Mobility Model (L) (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Mobility subnode for lattice (phonon) scattering: mu = mu0*(T/Tref)^(-alpha), with defaults for silicon (electron mobility reference 1448 cm^2/(V·s), exponent 2.33; hole reference 473 cm^2/(V·s)) and Tref 300 K, all From material. It is typically the first stage feeding other models (Fletcher, Arora, Caughey–Thomas) through their input-mobility settings.
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > right-click > Power Law Mobility Model (L); then select its output in the material model's Electron/Hole mobility lists
tools.example: Nonisothermal power diode: Power Law (L) -> Fletcher (C) -> Caughey–Thomas (E) chain, each using the previous model's output as its input mobility.
tools.notes: Letters in brackets indicate the effects included: L lattice, I ionized impurity, C carrier–carrier, E high field, S surface.

tools.name: Fletcher Mobility Model (C) (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Mobility subnode that adds carrier–carrier scattering, important at high injection (e.g. forward-biased power diodes and IGBTs), using the Fletcher formula with parameters F1 and F2 and an input mobility (typically from Power Law or Arora). Defaults are for silicon.
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > Fletcher Mobility Model (C). Java: feature("smm1").create("mmfl1", "FletcherMobilityModel", 2)

parameters.name: mun_in, mup_in
parameters.description: Input mobilities (default 1448 and 473 cm^2/(V·s) or another model's output).

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/pin_reverse_recovery: carrier–carrier scattering during high-level injection.
tools.notes: Chain with high-field (Caughey–Thomas) models last.

tools.name: Caughey–Thomas Mobility Model (E) (Semiconductor)
tools.description: High-field velocity-saturation mobility subnode: mu = mu_in/(1 + (mu_in*F/vsat)^beta)^(1/beta), with temperature-dependent saturation velocities and exponents (silicon defaults vn0 1e7 cm/s, vp0 8.37e6 cm/s) and a choice of driving force (e.g. field component parallel to the current). Usually applied last in the mobility chain for short-channel MOSFETs and high-voltage devices.
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > Caughey–Thomas Mobility Model (E). Java: feature("smm1").create("mmct1", "CaugheyThomasMobilityModel", 2); set("driving_force", "abs_Ep")
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/caughey_thomas_mobility and mosfet_mobility (drain current saturation).
tools.notes: Evaluate semi.mun_ct to inspect the resulting mobility.

tools.name: Lombardi Surface Mobility Model (S) (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Mobility subnode for surface (interface) scattering in MOSFET inversion layers, combining acoustic-phonon and surface-roughness terms that depend on the field normal to the current (the Lombardi model), with an input bulk mobility. Parameters deltan/deltap, mu1, mu2 and alpha are given for silicon.
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > Lombardi Surface Mobility Model (S). Java: feature("smm1").create("mmls1", "LombardiSurfaceMobilityModel", 2)

parameters.name: tolJ
parameters.description: Current density tolerance for the direction definition.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/lombardi_surface_mobility: Id-Vg curves with and without surface mobility degradation.
tools.notes: Requires a fine mesh in the inversion layer.

tools.name: Arora Mobility Model (LI) (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Mobility subnode combining lattice and ionized-impurity scattering (Arora model) as a function of temperature and total doping, with reference mobilities, minimum mobilities, reference doping concentrations and temperature exponents (silicon defaults: mun0 1252, mup0 407, mun_min 88, mup_min 54.3 cm^2/(V·s)).
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > Arora Mobility Model (LI). Java: feature("smm1").create("mmar1", "AroraMobilityModel", 2)
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/sic_diode_breakdown and Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/mosfet_mobility.
tools.notes: Klaassen (LIC) additionally includes carrier–carrier scattering.

tools.name: Klaassen Unified Mobility Model (LIC) (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Mobility subnode implementing the Klaassen unified model for silicon, which includes lattice scattering, ionized impurity scattering with screening and clustering, and electron–hole scattering in one consistent formulation; recommended for bipolar and power devices spanning wide doping and injection ranges. Parameters (mu_max, mu_min, theta, N_ref, alpha, c_D, c_A, f_BH, f_CW, fit coefficients s1..s7 and r1..r6) default to published silicon values.
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > Klaassen Unified Mobility Model (LIC). Java: feature("smm1").create("mmkl1", "KlaassenUnifiedMobilityModel", 2)
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/trench_gate_igbt_2d and trench_gate_igbt_3d.
tools.notes: Evaluate semi.mun_kl / semi.mup_kl to inspect results; chain with Caughey–Thomas for high fields.

tools.name: User-Defined Mobility Model (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Mobility subnode in which the electron and hole mobilities are arbitrary expressions (of temperature, doping, fields or input mobilities from other models), for materials or effects not covered by the built-in models. Its input mobility fields default to silicon values (1448 and 473 cm^2/(V·s)) or can reference outputs of other mobility subnodes.
tools.usage: Semiconductor Material Model > User-Defined Mobility Model

parameters.name: Electron/Hole input mobility
parameters.description: mu_n,in and mu_p,in (default silicon values or another model's output).

tools.example: Organic semiconductor with Poole–Frenkel mobility: mu_n = mu0*exp(gamma*sqrt(semi.normE)) in a User-Defined Mobility Model.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Metal Contact (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Boundary condition for metal–semiconductor contacts with terminal excitation Voltage (default 0 V), Current (0 A = open circuit), Circuit (current), Circuit (voltage) or Power. Contact type Ideal ohmic (default) or Ideal Schottky, where the barrier is ideal (metal work function minus electron affinity, default work function 4.5 V) or user defined, with thermionic currents via Richardson constants or surface recombination velocities and optional WKB tunneling extra current; an optional specific contact resistivity (default 1e-8 ohm·cm^2) adds a thin resistive layer.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Boundaries > Metal Contact. Java: physics("semi").create("mc1", "MetalContact", 1); set("ContactType", "Schottky"); set("Phi", "4.8[V]"); set("TerminalType", "Voltage"); set("V0", "Va")

parameters.name: TerminalName / TerminalType
parameters.description: Numeric name for sweeps; Voltage, Current, Circuit, CircuitVoltage, Power.

parameters.name: ContactType
parameters.description: ohmic or Schottky (SpecifyBarrierHeight ideal/userdef, Phi, Phi_B).

parameters.name: Astar_n, Astar_p / vsnin, vspin
parameters.description: Effective Richardson constants or recombination velocities.

parameters.name: extraElectronCurrent
parameters.description: WKBTunneling for tunneling through the barrier.

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/schottky_contact and cross_bridge_kelvin_resistor_contact_resistivity.
tools.notes: Terminal current is semi.I0_<name>. Supports exclusive Harmonic Perturbation for small-signal analysis.

tools.name: Thin Insulator Gate (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Boundary condition modelling a thin gate insulator of thickness d_ins and permittivity epsilon_ins between the semiconductor and a metal gate without meshing the oxide, e.g. MOSFET and MOSCAP gates. Terminal type Voltage (default), Charge (charge on the gate electrode, not the interface) or Circuit; gate contact settings include oxide permittivity and thickness and metal work function, plus density-gradient barrier options.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Boundaries > Thin Insulator Gate. Java: physics("semi").create("gc1", "GateContact", 1); set("V0", "Vg"); set("epsilon_ins", "3.9"); set("d_ins", "10[nm]"); set("Phi", "4.1[V]")
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/moscap_1d and moscap_1d_small_signal (C-V curve with a Harmonic Perturbation on the gate).
tools.notes: For thick or non-planar dielectrics model the oxide as a Charge Conservation domain (Insulator Interface applies automatically).

tools.name: Floating Gate (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Boundary feature (from the Electrostatics boundary submenu of the Semiconductor interface) for a gate electrode on a dielectric domain that is not connected to a source (or is connected to a circuit with floating potential). With a tunnel current from an Insulator Interface (e.g. Fowler–Nordheim) charge accumulates on the gate, modelling programming and erasing of flash/EEPROM cells; the contact work function and initial charge are specified.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Boundaries > Electrostatics > Floating Gate. Java: physics("semi").create("fg1", "FloatingGate", 1); set("I_tun", "..."); set("Q_init", "Qgate")

parameters.name: I_tun
parameters.description: Tunnel current: None, User defined or an Insulator Interface tunneling current.

parameters.name: Q_init
parameters.description: Initial gate charge (transient) or gate charge (stationary).

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/eeprom: control gate Terminal, floating gate charged by Fowler–Nordheim tunneling through the oxide in a Time Dependent study.
tools.notes: Requires explicit dielectric domains around the floating gate.

tools.name: Insulator Interface (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Boundary condition applied automatically at interfaces between Semiconductor Material Model domains and Charge Conservation (dielectric) domains. Its Tunneling setting adds None (default), Fowler–Nordheim tunneling (electrons, holes or both with A_FN and B_FN coefficients, e.g. 1.23e-6 A/V^2 and 237 MV/cm) or User-defined tunnel current densities; with the density-gradient formulation it also sets the barrier boundary condition.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Insulator Interface (default at semiconductor/insulator boundaries). Java: physics("semi").feature("ii1") (type InsulatorInterface); set("TunnelingType", "FowlerNordheim")
tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/eeprom (Fowler–Nordheim tunneling into the floating gate).
tools.notes: Surface traps at the interface are added with Trap-Assisted Surface Recombination (replaces the pre-5.4 Surface traps checkbox).

tools.name: Continuity/Heterojunction (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Default interior-boundary condition: inactive where material properties are continuous, and at heterojunctions it applies the chosen Continuity model: Continuous quasi-Fermi levels (default), Thermionic emission (carriers cross the band offset thermionically, optionally with an extra WKB tunneling current) or User-defined junction current (normal electron and hole currents specified directly).
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Continuity/Heterojunction (default on interior boundaries). Java: physics("semi").feature("cont1") (type Continuity); set("HeteroModelSelection", "2")

parameters.name: Continuity model (HeteroModelSelection)
parameters.description: Continuous quasi-Fermi levels, Thermionic emission, User-defined junction current.

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/heterojunction_1d (thermionic emission) and heterojunction_tunneling (WKB extra current).
tools.notes: Trap-Assisted Heterointerface Recombination adds interface traps (not with continuous quasi-Fermi levels).

tools.name: WKB Tunneling Model, Electrons / Holes (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Subnodes available when WKB tunneling is selected as the extra current of a heterojunction (thermionic emission) or Schottky Metal Contact; they compute the tunneling current density with the WKB approximation along field lines through a Potential barrier domain to an Opposite boundary. Inputs are the carrier effective mass and field-line/boundary coordinate expressions (often from a Curvilinear Coordinates solution) that parametrize the tunneling path.
tools.usage: Continuity/Heterojunction or Metal Contact (extra current: WKB tunneling model) > WKB Tunneling Model, Electrons. Java: feature("cont1").create("wkbe1", "WKBTunnelingModelElectrons", 1)

parameters.name: Opposite boundary selection
parameters.description: Exit side of the tunneling path.

parameters.name: flc, bndc
parameters.description: Field-line coordinate and boundary coordinate expressions.

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/mim_diode and Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/heterojunction_tunneling.
tools.notes: Add a thin domain adjacent to the junction to host the barrier when drawing the geometry.

tools.name: Optical Transitions (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Domain feature adding stimulated absorption/emission and spontaneous emission generation–recombination for direct band-gap semiconductors and computing the resulting change in complex refractive index/permittivity (with a Kramers–Kronig real-part correction). Transitions model: Direct band gap model (two-band model with Kane effective mass, spontaneous lifetime or matrix element) or User defined; the frequency domain can be represented in an extra dimension so spectra (e.g. emission vs. wavelength) are available.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Optical > Optical Transitions (added by default in the optoelectronics interfaces). Java: physics("semi").create("ot1", "OpticalTransitions", 2); set("TransitionsModel", "DirectBandGapModel")

parameters.name: MatrixElement / tau_spon
parameters.description: Spontaneous lifetime or momentum matrix element.

parameters.name: ExcitationFrequency / f0 / lambda0 / ElectricFieldNorm
parameters.description: Optical excitation when not coupled to an EM interface.

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/gaas_pn_junction_infrared_led_diode and gan_double_heterostructure_led (spontaneous emission spectra).
tools.notes: Couple to Electromagnetic Waves with the Semiconductor–Electromagnetic Waves Coupling (Wave Optics Module).

tools.name: Indirect Optical Transitions (Semiconductor)
tools.description: Domain feature for optical absorption and photogeneration in indirect band-gap materials: the refractive index (real and imaginary) is taken From material by default, from a built-in empirical silicon absorption model (frequency-dependent n and k), or from a user-defined absorption coefficient or extinction coefficient. The absorbed photon flux adds a carrier generation term; when coupled to an Electromagnetic Waves interface the refractive index and field intensity/frequency are exchanged automatically.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Optical > Indirect Optical Transitions

parameters.name: Transitions model
parameters.description: From material, Silicon empirical absorption, or User defined (absorption coefficient or imaginary index).

parameters.name: Optical excitation
parameters.description: Frequency and intensity (from the EM coupling or entered).

tools.example: Silicon photodiode under 850 nm illumination: Indirect Optical Transitions with the silicon model and an intensity of 1 kW/m^2, stationary photocurrent at reverse bias.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Semiconductor–Electrostatics Coupling
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling (sec1) that replaces the Semiconductor interface's built-in Poisson equation with the one from a separate Electrostatics interface on the selected domains, so advanced electrostatics constitutive models (for example Charge Conservation, Ferroelectric for ferroelectric FETs, or piezoelectric charge) act on the semiconductor.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Semiconductor–Electrostatics Coupling (when semi and es exist)

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: All domains (default) of the Semiconductor interface.

tools.example: Ferroelectric-gate FET: Electrostatics with Charge Conservation, Ferroelectric in the gate stack, Semiconductor channel, coupled with Semiconductor–Electrostatics Coupling to capture negative-capacitance behaviour.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Semiconductor Optoelectronics, Beam Envelopes / Frequency Domain (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined interfaces coupling the Semiconductor interface (with a default Optical Transitions node) to Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes or Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain through the Semiconductor–Electromagnetic Waves Coupling, so stimulated/spontaneous generation rates enter the carrier equations and the resulting gain/absorption feeds back into the optical field. They run with Frequency–Stationary, Frequency–Transient and Small-Signal Analysis studies in 2D and 3D (and 2D axisymmetric per the interface guide); a Wave Optics Module license is required.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Semiconductor > Semiconductor Optoelectronics, Beam Envelopes / Semiconductor Optoelectronics, Frequency Domain
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/gaas_pin_photodiode (ewfd + semi) and silicon_on_insulator_modulator (Mode Analysis + carrier-induced index change).
tools.notes: Requires both the Semiconductor and Wave Optics Modules.

tools.name: Semiconductor–Electromagnetic Waves Coupling
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling (semc1) that passes the optical field intensity from an electromagnetic waves interface to the Optical Transitions (or Indirect Optical Transitions) feature of the Semiconductor interface and returns the change in complex refractive index or permittivity from absorption/gain to the electromagnetic interface. It is added automatically by the Semiconductor Optoelectronics multiphysics interfaces.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Semiconductor–Electromagnetic Waves Coupling. Java: multiphysics().create("semc1", "SemiconductorElectromagneticWavesCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: All domains with an active Optical Transitions feature.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/gaas_pin_photodiode: photocurrent versus optical power at 870 nm.
tools.notes: Requires the Wave Optics Module.

tools.name: Schrödinger Equation (schr)
tools.description: Solves the single-particle Schrödinger equation (envelope-function approximation) for the wave function of electrons or holes in an external potential, for quantum wells, wires, dots, superlattices, tunneling structures and even Gross–Pitaevskii condensates. Supports Eigenvalue (eigenenergies), Stationary and Time Dependent studies in all space dimensions; default nodes are Effective Mass, Electron Potential Energy, Zero Flux and Initial Values, and multicomponent wave functions allow k·p Hamiltonians.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Semiconductor > Schrödinger Equation. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("schr", "SchrodingerEquation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Particle type
parameters.description: Electrons (default) or Holes (sign convention of potential energy).

parameters.name: Eigenvalue scale
parameters.description: Energy scale for the eigenvalue solver (e.g. 1 eV).

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/double_barrier_1d (resonant tunneling), Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/solving_hydrogen_atom and superlattice_band_gap_tool.
tools.notes: Results: schr.Ei (eigenenergy), schr.Pr (probability density), schr.Psi. Energies are entered in J with eV units, e.g. 0.1[eV].

tools.name: Effective Mass / Electron Potential Energy (Schrödinger Equation)
tools.description: Default domain nodes of the Schrödinger Equation: Effective Mass sets the particle's effective mass tensor (defaults 0.067*me_const for electrons, 0.45*me_const for holes; later nodes override earlier ones for heterostructures), and Electron Potential Energy adds a contribution to the total potential energy using a Simple harmonic potential (default), Quantum well (width 10 nm, depth 100 meV) or User defined expression; contributions from several nodes add up.
tools.usage: Schrödinger Equation > Effective Mass (type EffectiveMass) / Electron Potential Energy (type ElectronPotentialEnergy). Java: physics("schr").feature("meff1").set("meff", "0.067*me_const")

parameters.name: meff
parameters.description: Effective mass (isotropic, diagonal, symmetric or full).

parameters.name: Ve profile
parameters.description: Simple harmonic (omega0, r0, V0), Quantum well (d0, Vw, center) or user defined.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/si_inversion_layer_density_gradient_and_schrodinger_poisson: Electron Potential Energy from the electrostatic potential via the Schrödinger–Poisson coupling.
tools.notes: For holes the potential energy sign convention is reversed (particles float up).

tools.name: Hamiltonian terms for k·p models (Schrödinger Equation)
tools.description: Domain conditions for multicomponent wave functions that build general matrix Hamiltonians term by term: Second Order Hamiltonian, First Order Hamiltonian (Left and Right) and Zeroth Order Hamiltonian, each with a table of row/column indices, differential operators and parameters. They implement k·p models (e.g. 6x6 wurtzite valence bands), spin terms and Zeeman splitting.
tools.usage: Schrödinger Equation (multicomponent) > Second Order Hamiltonian (type SecondOrderHamiltonianSemicond) / First Order Hamiltonian, Left/Right / Zeroth Order Hamiltonian (type ZerothOrderHamiltonianSemicond)

parameters.name: A parameter / Description
parameters.description: Coefficient of the term (built-in factor hbar^2/(2*me) for second order).

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/k_dot_p_method_strained_wurtzite_gan_band_structure; Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/si_quantum_dot_in_uniform_magnetic_field uses Zeroth Order Hamiltonian for spin.
tools.notes: Primarily for multicomponent wave functions; single-component models use Effective Mass and Electron Potential Energy.

tools.name: Zero Flux / Zero Probability / Open Boundary / Periodic Condition (Schrödinger Equation)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of the Schrödinger Equation: Zero Flux (default, natural condition, zero normal probability current), Zero Probability (psi = 0, hard wall), Open Boundary (non-reflecting outgoing plane, cylindrical or spherical wave with optional incoming wave, single-component only) and Periodic Condition (Floquet periodicity with a wave vector for superlattice band structures).
tools.usage: Schrödinger Equation > Boundaries > Zero Flux (type ZeroFlux) / Zero Probability (ZeroProbability) / Open Boundary (OpenBoundary) / Periodic Condition (PeriodicCondition)
tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Verification_Examples/double_barrier_1d: Open Boundary with an incoming wave to compute transmission versus energy.
tools.notes: For stationary scattering problems a Perfectly Matched Layer is an alternative to Open Boundary.

tools.name: Lorentz Force / Rotating Frame / Dissipation (Schrödinger Equation)
tools.description: Additional domain terms of the Schrödinger Equation: Lorentz Force adds the magnetic vector potential of a uniform or given magnetic field to the Hamiltonian (Landau levels, quantum dots in B fields); Rotating Frame adds the rotation term for rotating condensates; Dissipation adds a phenomenological damping term for time-dependent relaxation (e.g. vortex lattice formation in Gross–Pitaevskii models).
tools.usage: Schrödinger Equation > Lorentz Force (type LorentzForce_schr) / Rotating Frame (RotatingFrameSchrod) / Dissipation (DissipationSchrod)
tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/si_quantum_dot_in_uniform_magnetic_field (Lorentz Force) and vortex_lattice_formation_in_a_rotating_bose_einstein_condensate (Rotating Frame + Dissipation).
tools.notes: Nonlinear Gross–Pitaevskii terms are added with an Electron Potential Energy depending on |psi|^2 (Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/gross_pitaevskii_equation_for_bose_einstein_condensation).

tools.name: Schrödinger–Poisson Equation (multiphysics interface and coupling)
tools.description: Predefined interface that bidirectionally couples Electrostatics and Schrödinger Equation through the Schrödinger–Poisson Coupling (schrp1): the electric potential enters the Schrödinger potential energy, and a statistically weighted (Fermi–Dirac occupied) sum of eigenstate probability densities becomes space charge in Poisson's equation. Used for self-consistent quantum confinement in inversion layers, nanowires and heterostructures in all space dimensions, solved with the dedicated Schrödinger–Poisson study.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Semiconductor > Schrödinger–Poisson Equation (adds es, schr and schrp1). Java: multiphysics().create("schrp1", "SchrodingerPoissonCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: Charge / statistics settings
parameters.description: Particle charge, degeneracy, Fermi level and temperature for occupation.

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Overlap of the Schrödinger and Electrostatics selections (default All domains).

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/schrodinger_poisson_nanowire and Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/si_inversion_layer_density_gradient_and_schrodinger_poisson (compared with density-gradient).
tools.notes: For device-level quantum corrections with currents use the density-gradient formulation of the Semiconductor interface.

tools.name: Schrödinger–Poisson (study step)
tools.description: Dedicated study step that generates the self-consistent iteration between an Eigenvalue solve of the Schrödinger Equation and a Stationary solve of Electrostatics in the solver sequence. The default eigenvalue search method is Manual (find the energy range and number of states first), after which Region search with suitable energy range and count ensures all significant states are captured; the Unit list must stay blank.
tools.usage: Add Study > Schrödinger–Poisson (from the Model Wizard or Add Study to get physics-suggested defaults). Java: model.study("std1").create("sdpo", "SchrodingerPoisson")

parameters.name: Search region / number of eigenvalues
parameters.description: Energy window and maximum count (real/imaginary parts refer to the eigenvalue).

parameters.name: Iteration settings
parameters.description: Tolerance and damping of the self-consistent loop in the solver sequence.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Quantum_Systems/schrodinger_poisson_nanowire: parametric sweep of gate voltage around the Schrödinger–Poisson study.
tools.notes: A study step added by right-clicking the Study node does not get the physics-suggested defaults.

tools.name: Semiconductor Equilibrium (study step)
tools.description: Study and study step that compute the semiconductor solution under thermal equilibrium by solving only Poisson's equation (with carrier and ionized-dopant space charge), the most efficient solution for systems known to be in equilibrium and a robust initial condition for nonequilibrium studies. All metal contacts on the same Semiconductor Material Model share a common bias set by the material model's Equilibrium condition (Bias voltage or Total charge).
tools.usage: Add Study > Semiconductor Equilibrium. Java: model.study("std1").create("semie", "SemiconductorEquilibrium")

parameters.name: Equilibrium condition
parameters.description: Set in the Semiconductor Material Model (V0_bias or Q0_tot).

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: As for a Stationary study step (parametric sweeps allowed).

tools.example: Application Libraries Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/moscap_1d and mim_diode: Semiconductor Equilibrium sweep of gate bias for C-V without solving carrier currents.
tools.notes: Only valid when no net current flows; use Stationary for biased devices, seeded with the equilibrium solution.

tools.name: Semiconductor Initialization (study step)
tools.description: Study step that adaptively refines the mesh according to the gradient of the impurity doping concentration: it solves an auxiliary (unphysical) equation with adaptive mesh refinement switched on by default, producing a mesh concentrated at junctions before the device equations are solved. Settings are similar to a Stationary step.
tools.usage: Add Study > Semiconductor Initialization (then add Stationary/Time Dependent steps using the refined mesh). Java: model.study("std1").create("semii", "SemiconductorInitialization")

parameters.name: Adaptation
parameters.description: Adaptive mesh refinement settings (on by default).

parameters.name: Follow-up steps
parameters.description: Use the adapted mesh in later study steps.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Photonic_Devices_and_Sensors/gaas_pn_junction_infrared_led_diode: Semiconductor Initialization before the forward-bias sweep.
tools.notes: Available with the Semiconductor Module.

tools.name: Nonisothermal semiconductor models (Total heat source semi)
tools.description: Procedure for electro-thermal device simulation: add Heat Transfer in Solids, apply a Heat Source using the Semiconductor interface's 'Total heat source (semi)' (Joule heating plus recombination heat) for a one-way coupling, then set the Semiconductor Material Model temperature input to Temperature (ht) for a fully coupled model, preferably initialized with the one-way solution. Mobility and recombination models then follow the local temperature.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Solids > Heat Source > General source Q: Total heat source (semi); Semiconductor Material Model > Model Inputs > Temperature: Temperature (ht)

parameters.name: Heat source
parameters.description: Total heat source (semi): Joule plus recombination heating (simplified model).

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/bipolar_transistor_thermal: self-heating of a BJT and its effect on the output characteristics.
tools.notes: Thermoelectric (Peltier/Seebeck) heat is not part of the simplified heat source.

tools.name: Semiconductor result variables (semi.N, semi.P, semi.Ec_e, semi.Efn_e, semi.I0_1)
tools.description: Key postprocessing variables of the Semiconductor interface: carrier concentrations semi.N and semi.P (and semi.log10N/log10P), doping semi.Nd, semi.Na, net doping semi.Nnetdop and ionized dopants semi.Ndplus/semi.Naminus, band diagram energies in eV semi.Ec_e, semi.Ev_e, quasi-Fermi levels semi.Efn_e, semi.Efp_e, current densities semi.JnX, semi.JpX, semi.JX, semi.normJ, field semi.normE, terminal currents/voltages semi.I0_<n>, semi.V0_<n>, mobilities such as semi.mun_ct, and impact generation semi.Gii.
tools.usage: Results > Line Graph of semi.Ec_e, semi.Ev_e, semi.Efn_e, semi.Efp_e along a cut line (band diagram); Global Evaluation of semi.I0_1 for I-V curves

parameters.name: I0_<n>
parameters.description: Terminal current of contact <n> (per unit thickness in 2D if thickness not set).

tools.example: Band diagram: Line Graph with expressions semi.Ec_e, semi.Ev_e, semi.Efn_e, semi.Efp_e on a Cut Line through the junction; I-V: 1D Global plot of semi.I0_1 versus Va.
tools.notes: Names confirmed from expressions in the 6.4 Semiconductor Application Library.

tools.name: Insulation / Zero Charge / Electric Potential (Semiconductor default boundaries)
tools.description: Default exterior conditions of the Semiconductor interface: Insulation (no carrier current through the boundary) and Zero Charge (no displacement flux, n·D = 0), together forming an electrically insulating, charge-free surface. Electrostatics-type boundary nodes such as Electric Potential, Surface Charge Density, Electric Displacement Field and Floating Gate can be added from the Electrostatics submenu to set field-plate or guard-ring potentials on insulating regions.
tools.usage: Semiconductor > Insulation / Zero Charge (defaults); Boundaries > Electrostatics > Electric Potential / Surface Charge Density. Java: physics("semi").create("pot1", "ElectricPotential", 1)

parameters.name: Insulation
parameters.description: Zero normal electron and hole current.

tools.example: Application Library Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/sic_diode_breakdown: Electric Potential on field-contact rings ('Anode field contact') on the passivation.
tools.notes: Metal Contact and Thin Insulator Gate are used for electrodes touching the semiconductor itself.
